clue.text: Barrier backed by head of state against some of our freedoms

definitions.text: Barrier backed by head of state against some of our freedoms

indicators.note: against means next to, so the liberties fragment sits up against the rest
some of means only part of the word is used, here its opening four letters

parts.note: our freedoms are our liberties

indicators.note: backed means turned round, so the barrier word is read from its end to its start

parts.note: a wall is a barrier

indicators.note: head of picks out the opening letter of the word state

explanation.surface: A complaint that a wall, endorsed by the head of state, is being built against some of our freedoms.
explanation.walkthrough: Indicators: 'backed' reverses the barrier, 'head of' takes a first letter, 'some of' trims the liberties, and 'against' sets that trimmed piece alongside, in front. Read whole, the clue describes laws restraining free speech.
explanation.definitionFit: Laws of defamation act as a barrier restricting freedom of speech and the press, as the whole clue suggests.

clue.text: Tables entered by 14 across

definitions.meaning: a fighter enters the tournament arena

explanation.walkthrough: The lists were the arena where knights jousted, so a combatant enters them.
explanation.definitionFit: Lists are tables of items, and also the enclosed ground of a medieval tournament.

clue.text: Application of water or fire is pursuant upon fitting in British Museum

indicators.note: in puts the fitting pieces inside the museum's initials
pursuant upon means following, so is comes after fitting

parts.note: apt means fitting

explanation.surface: Fire and water at the British Museum, following a fitting.
explanation.walkthrough: The Bible speaks of baptism by water and by fire (Matthew 3:11).
explanation.definitionFit: Baptism is the sacrament of washing with water, and scripture also speaks of a baptism of fire.

clue.text: Mecca for cricketers with joint title

parts.note: Lord's, the London cricket ground, is the game's spiritual home
the hip is a joint of the body

explanation.surface: A cricket ground with a jointly held name.
explanation.walkthrough: LORD'S is the famous London cricket ground, home of the MCC.
explanation.definitionFit: A form of address for a peer or judge, as in 'Your Lordship', is a title of rank.

clue.text: Relative's friend put up to be put down

definitions.text: put up to be put down

parts.note: a relative, and the possessive gives the s
an ally is a friend

explanation.surface: A relative's friend is set up only to be knocked down.
explanation.walkthrough: An Aunt Sally is a fairground figure set up for throwing things at, so anyone set up as an easy target.
explanation.definitionFit: A target, literal or figurative, erected only so others can knock it over or criticise it.

clue.text: Such shoes are for soldiers gathered round wild tree without oxygen

indicators.note: gathered round says the soldiers' word encloses the rest

parts.note: a squad is a small group of soldiers

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the shuffled tree surrounds oxygen
wild suggests the letters of tree run riot into a new order

parts.note: O is the chemical symbol for oxygen

explanation.surface: Soldiers gather round a wild tree that lacks oxygen to describe their shoes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like 'lacking' but is the old sense 'outside': the shuffled tree (from 'wild') wraps the oxygen symbol, giving RETOE, and 'gathered round' puts the soldiers around all that.
explanation.definitionFit: Square-toed describes footwear with a blunt, squared-off front, an old-fashioned style.

clue.text: Pleasing sound of catcall not well received

indicators.note: received means heard, so the words are taken as spoken rather than as spelt

parts.note: a catcall is a mew, and not well is sick

explanation.surface: A heckler's catcall at a concert gets a poor reception.
explanation.walkthrough: 'received' tells you to say MEW SICK out loud; spoken, it sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Melody and harmony are the pleasing sounds we enjoy hearing, the stuff of concerts and songs.

clue.text: Apply fertiliser at risk from 1 across?

definitions.meaning: spreading scandal is what defamation laws punish

explanation.walkthrough: Muck-spreading is also slang for spreading scurrilous stories, which risks a libel action.
explanation.definitionFit: Farmers spread manure on the land, and scandal-mongers spread dirt about people.

clue.text: Hard stuff is cheerful

definitions.meaning: to spirit is to cheer, an old verb sense

explanation.walkthrough: Chambers gives the verb 'spirit' meaning to cheer up; the link is a stretch.
explanation.definitionFit: Whisky and gin are strong drinks, and the verb 'spirit' can mean to cheer or enliven.

clue.text: Vessel on 10, perhaps

definitions.meaning: a big box carried aboard a cargo vessel

explanation.walkthrough: 10 is SHIP: freight boxes travel on container ships.
explanation.definitionFit: A receptacle is a vessel, and big freight boxes travel on cargo vessels.

clue.text: Drink to Ireland at get-together with gag upon gag

parts.note: to sup is to drink
Erin is a poetic name for Ireland
a junction is a meeting or joining point

explanation.surface: Someone toasts Ireland at a party, telling joke after joke.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gag' looks like a joke but means a court order silencing the press; this order also bans reporting that the order exists, so it is a gag on a gag.
explanation.definitionFit: A super-injunction is a court order that forbids reporting of the matter and of the order's own existence, a doubled silencing.

clue.text: See 3
Playgirl put plant on mount

parts.note: cress is a salad plant
Mount Ida is a mountain in Crete and another near Troy

explanation.surface: A good-time girl puts a plant on top of a mountain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Playgirl' is read as a girl in a play: the heroine of Shakespeare's Troilus and Cressida. 'on' simply joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare wrote a play named after the Trojan lovers, so she is literally a girl from a play.

clue.text: Right lot of terrorists turn in the dirt, being experts on 1 across

indicators.note: in places the run of pieces inside the dirt word

parts.note: cack is slang for dirt or excrement

indicators.note: a lot of means most but not all, so only the opening of the word is kept

parts.note: a U-turn, so U stands for a turn

explanation.surface: Most of a gang of terrorists turn up in the dirt, experts on the subject.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dirt' tempts MUCK, but it is CACK. Carter-Ruck is a London law firm famous for libel cases; 'lot of' trims terrorists to TERR.
explanation.definitionFit: The firm of solicitors founded by Peter Carter-Ruck is renowned for defamation work.

clue.text: Indian music on mule for urchin

indicators.note: on in a down clue puts the music above the mule

parts.note: a raga is a pattern of Indian classical music
Muffin the Mule was a puppet on early British children's television

explanation.surface: Indian music played on a mule for a street child.
explanation.walkthrough: Muffin the Mule was a puppet on 1950s BBC children's television.
explanation.definitionFit: A ragamuffin is a ragged, dirty child, a street urchin.

clue.text: Fighter for flier in trance not cut short

indicators.note: in places the flier inside the word for a trance

parts.note: a coma is a deep trance-like unconsciousness
a bat is a flying mammal
not shortened is the contraction n't, as in can't

explanation.surface: A fighter pilot in a trance who is not cut short.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flier' suggests a pilot, but it is the animal BAT.
explanation.definitionFit: A combatant is one who takes part in fighting, a warrior or belligerent.

clue.text: Drink to truce breaker amid applause

indicators.note: amid places the broken truce inside the applause

parts.note: a clap is applause

indicators.note: breaker means the word truce is broken up and reassembled

explanation.surface: A toast to the end of a ceasefire, amid applause.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breaker' rearranges TRUCE to RETCU.
explanation.definitionFit: Claret cup is a punch made of red wine with fruit, a drink.

clue.text: Amber has stake on fictional horse

parts.note: rosin is a resin, and amber is fossil resin of the same colour
an ante is a stake in poker

explanation.surface: A gambler named Amber backs a horse in a novel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Amber' looks like a name; it is the resin.
explanation.definitionFit: Don Quixote's bony old nag in Cervantes's novel is the most famous fictional steed.

clue.text: A green meaning "stop"?

parts.note: vert is green in heraldry

explanation.surface: A traffic light shows green, yet it means stop.
explanation.walkthrough: VERT is the heraldic word for green; 'meaning' just links wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To avert something is to prevent it, to stop it from happening.

clue.text: Part of rope's part of grass

indicators.note: Part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A grass forming a component of a rope.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'Part of' is the signal; the second is part of the text the run of letters is taken from, crossing all three words.
explanation.definitionFit: Esparto is a tough grass of Spain and North Africa used for rope and paper.

clue.text: Great king and queen following a drink with a kiss

indicators.note: following means the 'and queen' pieces come after the drink and kiss

parts.note: ale is a drink
X stands for a kiss at the end of a letter
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: A king and queen follow a drink with a kiss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Great' belongs to the definition, Alexander the Great, not to the wordplay; 'following' puts the 'and queen' pieces after the drink and kiss.
explanation.definitionFit: Alexander the Great was the Macedonian king who conquered an empire.

clue.text: Show red card to underworld girl

parts.note: Dis is the Roman god of the underworld, and his realm
a miss is a girl

explanation.surface: A referee sends off a girl from the underworld.
explanation.definitionFit: A football referee showing the red card sends a player off, so the player is dismissed.

clue.text: Backward Guardian diarist to work at setter's shop

indicators.note: Backward tells you to read the whole run of pieces from the end

parts.note: Hugh Muir wrote the Guardian's diary column
op is short for opus, a work
the setter refers to himself as me

explanation.surface: A Guardian diarist goes backwards to work at the setter's shop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backward' reverses MUIR + OP + ME as one run. Hugh Muir wrote the Guardian newspaper's diary column at the time.
explanation.definitionFit: An emporium is a large store or trading place selling many goods.

clue.text: Deity has two lives

indicators.note: two means the piece is used twice in a row

parts.note: to live is to exist, so lives can be is

explanation.surface: A god possessed of a pair of lives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lives' is the verb: he lives, he is.
explanation.definitionFit: Isis was a major goddess of ancient Egypt, worshipped as a mother figure.

clue.text: See 4
Bird heard from bird

definitions.meaning: a black bird of the genus Corvus

explanation.definitionFit: The crow is a common black bird, and a crow is a cock's call.

clue.text: See 15
Miracle cure, if time allows, around a point of the compass

definitions.text: Miracle cure, if time allows, around a point of the compass

indicators.note: around puts the shuffled letters round the compass point
allows in the sense of makes possible a new arrangement of the letters before it

parts.note: N, for north, is a point of the compass

explanation.surface: A miracle cure, time permitting, found near a compass point.
explanation.walkthrough: 'allows' rearranges MIRACLE CURE IF T, and 'around' puts that round N. The whole clue also pictures a circle drawn round the point of a pair of compasses.
explanation.definitionFit: Circumferential means lying on or relating to the perimeter of a circle, as drawn around a compass point.

clue.text: Put down wine (but not this?)

definitions.meaning: cheap wine, the sort you would not lay down to mature

explanation.walkthrough: 'Put down' also suggests laying down wine to age; cheap table wine is the one kind you would not.
explanation.definitionFit: To plonk is to set down heavily, and plonk is slang for cheap, rough wine.

clue.text: State request from wool shop?

definitions.meaning: a customer at a knitwear shop might ask for a fresh pullover

explanation.walkthrough: A jersey is a knitted pullover, so a shopper might ask for a new one.
explanation.definitionFit: New Jersey is a state of the USA, and a new jersey is what a woolly-jumper buyer wants.
